title: Key got stuck when alternate(latch) key is mapped for physical key

status.label: Reproduce stuck Japanese IME key remaps
status.detail: The report describes VK242/VK245 remaps remaining logically pressed on a Japanese keyboard; related tracker #3397 covers a similar stuck-key symptom with Japanese IME.

judgment.rationale: The issue identifies the Japanese keyboard environment, VK242/VK245 source keys, and a stuck-key consequence that persists until locking and unlocking the screen. A commenter reports that VK242 can leave an Alt remap held and cites multi-key events from the JIS layout. Open issue #3397 describes a related stuck remap under Japanese IME, but its Caps Lock/VK240 case does not prove that these source keys share the same failure path.
evidence: The reporter describes remapping VK242/VK245 and says the resulting key can remain pressed until the screen is locked and unlocked.
A commenter reports a related VK242-to-Alt+PrintScreen case and notes the issue occurs with a JIS-specific key.
Issue #3397 remains open for a related remapped-key-stays-pressed failure when switching to Japanese IME.
No maintainer reproduction or current PowerToys version is present in this issue.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce VK242/VK245 source mappings on a JIS keyboard with Japanese IME enabled, distinguish source-key and destination-key release events, and compare the result with #3397 without treating the reports as identical.

fix_assessment.rationale: A code fix may need to preserve balanced key-up state for JIS/IME-generated multi-key events. The related tracker #3397 is not a confirmed fix or duplicate for VK242/VK245 remaps.

proposed_fixes.title: Balance key state for Japanese IME toggle-key remaps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The JIS keyboard or Japanese IME may emit multiple virtual-key transitions for a toggle key, while Keyboard Manager tracks only the remapped key's expected down/up sequence; this is a hypothesis pending reproduction.
plan: Reproduce the VK242/VK245-to-physical-key mappings with Japanese IME active and record which source and destination key events remain down.
Compare the event sequence with the stuck Caps Lock remap in open issue #3397 to determine whether the same IME transition is involved.
If Keyboard Manager leaves injected key state unmatched, update its event tracking to release the remapped key on all source-key and IME transition paths.
Add regression tests for both release orders and for the JIS toggle-key event sequence.
verification: VK242/VK245 remaps release cleanly after each press on a JIS keyboard with Japanese IME enabled.
Switching input mode and using unrelated keys does not leave a modifier or remapped key held.
Existing Japanese IME and ordinary-layout remapping tests continue to pass.

confidence.rationale: The issue and related reports establish a concrete stuck-key symptom, but there is no maintainer reproduction or event trace proving the exact shared state failure.

issue_context.summary: On a Japanese keyboard, remapping VK242/VK245 reportedly leaves a key logically pressed until the screen is locked and unlocked.
known_information: The issue body reports PowerToys 0.57.2 and a Japanese keyboard.
The reporter describes remapping VK242/VK245 and a stuck-key effect.
A commenter reports a similar VK242 source-key failure with an Alt remap.
Open issue #3397 tracks a related stuck remapped key while changing to Japanese IME, but uses a different source-key case.
inferences: The problem may involve JIS/IME-generated multiple virtual-key events and unmatched key state; this has not been confirmed for this mapping.
issue_context.analysis: The related tracker is useful counterevidence and a comparison point, but it does not establish a fix or complete coverage. A focused reproduction of the specific VK242/VK245 mapping is needed before merging or rerouting the reports.
initial_investigation: Read the issue and all three comments, including the report's key description and the related links to #3397 and #13955.
Reviewed #3397 and its Japanese IME discussion; it remains open and concerns a distinct Caps Lock/VK240 scenario.
No current-version confirmation or maintainer reproduction is documented.

information_gaps.information: Whether the VK242/VK245 remap still sticks on current stable, and the exact source and destination mapping used
information_gaps.why_needed: This confirms the old report remains current and determines which key-up transitions must be exercised.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm the current PowerToys version, Japanese IME mode, whether the logical layout is JIS/kbd106, and one exact VK242 or VK245 source-to-destination mapping that reproduces the stuck state.

actions.label: Confirm the current JIS key mapping

comment.body: Your report describes VK242/VK245 remaps sticking on a Japanese keyboard. Could you confirm whether this still happens on current stable, which exact source-to-destination mapping reproduces it, and whether the Windows logical layout is JIS/kbd106 with Japanese IME active?

reproduce.title: Check VK242/VK245 key release under Japanese IME
prerequisites: JIS keyboard or Windows JIS/kbd106 logical layout
setup: Configure a VK242 or VK245 source key to a physical destination key, recording the exact mapping.
steps: Press and release the mapped source key while Japanese IME is active.
Use unrelated keys and check whether the remapped key or modifier remains held.
Repeat while changing the IME mode and with the alternative VK242/VK245 key if available.
Compare with the same destination mapping from an ordinary non-toggle source key.
reproduce.expected_result: Each source press produces the configured destination action and returns all remapped key state to released without locking or unlocking the screen.

actions.label: Approve the Japanese IME key-state investigation
